text: Iestyn George is a Welsh journalist who previously served as an editor at NME and GQ, and is currently a lecturer at the University of Brighton. During the 1990s, he wrote for NME and later became its news editor. Between 1999 and 2003, he held the position of marketing manager for the Welsh band the Manic Street Preachers. By 2001, he was also appointed music editor at GQ magazine and became deputy editor at Golf Punk magazine. In 2009, he became editor of Rio magazine, which was founded by Manchester United player Rio Ferdinand, who served as editor-in-chief. Iestyn George is the son of Welsh broadcaster Beti George and is the brother-in-law of Tim Southwell, the co-founder of Loaded and founder of Golf Punk.
